translation.response: 人们常常根据预测最终是否成真来评价一个计划，但即使未来与预期不同，一个有用的计划仍可能保持价值。
人们往往以预测最终是否应验来评价一项计划；不过，即使实际发生的未来没有符合原先的预期，一个有用的计划仍然可能继续发挥作用。
人们常常用预测是否正确来判断计划，但未来不同的时候计划也可能有一些价值。
计划只有在预测完全正确时才真正有价值，因此只要未来偏离预期，原来的计划就失去了意义。
预测正确，计划有价值，未来不同。

writing_small.response:
Dear Coordinator,
I am writing to request a short extension for the project report due on Monday. The university laboratory I need has unexpectedly been closed for two days, so I cannot complete the final part of the report on time. Would it be possible for me to submit it by Wednesday evening instead? I understand that changing the deadline may cause inconvenience, and I will finish the report as soon as the laboratory reopens. If there are any forms I should complete for the extension, please let me know.
Thank you for your consideration.
Yours sincerely,
Li Ming

Dear Coordinator,
I hope this message finds you well. Unfortunately, the university laboratory has been closed unexpectedly for two days. This situation has caused considerable difficulty for the completion of my report, and I sincerely apologize for any inconvenience that may result. I have reviewed the parts I can complete without the laboratory and will continue working on them in the meantime. I value the course requirements and hope the unexpected closure will not create unnecessary trouble for the teaching schedule. I greatly appreciate your patience and understanding and will continue to work diligently on the project.
Yours sincerely,
Li Ming

Dear Coordinator,
The laboratory I need for my report has been closed for two days, so I cannot finish the report by Monday. Could I hand it in on Wednesday evening instead? I am sorry for the inconvenience and will complete the remaining work as soon as the lab opens again. I have already finished the parts that do not need the lab. I will use the next two days to check my notes, so I can finish quickly when the lab opens.
Thank you for considering my request.
Yours sincerely,
Li Ming

Dear teacher,
The lab close for two days and my report Monday is difficult to finish. I want more time because I cannot do the experiment now. I am sorry for this problem. Please give me some more days. I will try hard and finish the work quickly when the lab open again. I hope you can understand my situation. I know the report is important and I do not want make trouble for the course. Thank you very much for help me.
Li Ming

writing_big.response:
The picture contrasts two ways of dealing with abundant online information. One student keeps collecting links without deciding which sources deserve trust, while the other begins with a clear question, compares evidence and relevance, and then makes a decision. The contrast suggests that access to more information is useful only when it is guided by judgment.

Information itself does not remove uncertainty. In fact, collecting material without a decision rule can make a person slower because every new source creates another option to examine. A clear question, however, narrows the search and gives the reader a basis for comparing evidence. This is why effective research depends not only on finding information but also on deciding what information is relevant and credible.

In study and work, therefore, people should treat search as part of a decision process rather than as an end in itself. Better judgment, not a larger pile of links, turns information into useful knowledge. That discipline also makes later revision easier because the reasons for a choice remain visible.

The picture shows two students using the Internet in different ways. This tells us that judgment is very important in our life. As we all know, judgment is the key to success. Without good judgment, people cannot make progress. With good judgment, people can solve many problems and achieve their dreams. Many successful people in history had good judgment, so they became successful. Therefore, every young person should improve judgment and work hard. Only in this way can we create a better future and become useful people for society.

Good judgment also helps us face difficulties at school and at work. When we have judgment, we can choose the right direction and avoid wasting time. Society is changing rapidly, so young people need this quality more than ever. Families and schools should teach students to think carefully, and students should learn from successful examples around them. If everyone develops better judgment, our society will become more efficient, harmonious and hopeful.

The illustration demonstrates that students should collect as much information as possible before making any decision. The first student opens many sources and therefore has a broader vision, whereas the second student limits the search too early and risks missing valuable evidence. In modern society, success belongs to those who gather the greatest amount of knowledge. The more information one owns, the more objective one's judgment becomes. For this reason, universities should encourage students to read widely and postpone decisions until they have explored every possible source.

Large information sets also reduce the danger of personal bias, because conclusions can be tested against more viewpoints. By contrast, a narrow search may create false confidence and lock a student into the first attractive explanation. Patience in gathering evidence is therefore not indecision but intellectual responsibility. The safest decision is one made only after the available informational field has been exhausted as fully as possible. In this view, delaying closure is a sign of careful thinking.

The two students have the same information, but they use it differently. One keeps saving links and does not decide what is useful. The other first asks a clear question and then compares a few sources before making a decision. The picture shows that more information is not always better if we do not know how to judge it.

A clear purpose helps us choose useful evidence. For example, when students prepare a paper, they may waste hours reading unrelated material. If they know the exact question, they can compare sources and spend more time thinking about the answer. Good judgment therefore saves time and improves the quality of a decision.

We should not stop searching too early, but we should also know why we are searching. Information becomes useful only when it supports a clear decision. This does not mean that students should ignore new evidence. If a useful source challenges their first answer, they should revise it. The point is to search with a purpose, not to count how many links they have saved.

There are two students in the picture. Internet is very important today. We can learn many things from Internet. Students should use Internet every day. It makes life convenient and gives us knowledge. We should study hard and use technology correctly. Technology can help our country develop. In conclusion, Internet is good and we should use it well.

Nowadays almost everyone has a phone and can find information very quickly. Teachers can use websites in class, and students can watch videos after class. The Internet also makes communication easier, because people can send messages and share files. Of course, there can be some bad information online, so students should be careful. Parents and schools should guide young people to use the Internet in a healthy way. If we use technology correctly, it will bring more convenience to study, work and daily life and help society make progress. Therefore, learning to use the Internet is an important task for every student today.

The two students use the same online information in different ways. One keeps collecting links without deciding what is useful, while the other starts with a clear question and compares evidence before making a decision. The picture shows that information needs judgment.

A clear purpose helps people avoid wasting time on irrelevant sources. It also makes comparison easier because they know what evidence matters. Students should still remain open to new evidence, but they should search for a reason instead of collecting links without a decision rule.

responses.response: 人们往往以预测最终是否应验来评价一项计划；不过，即使实际发生的未来没有符合原先的预期，一个有用的计划仍然可能继续发挥作用。
它更深层的作用是把各种假设显现出来，使人们能够注意到哪些变化真正需要他们采取不同的行动。
当人们必须在所有相关信息尚未齐备之前作出决定时，这一点尤其重要，而在受控实验之外通常就是如此。
一个已经明确在什么条件下应当改变策略的团队，就不太容易把一味坚持误认为纪律性。
因此，目标并不是消除不确定性，而是设计出能够对不确定性作出明智回应的决策。
